title: Detailed telemetry pipeline for semantic rankers and route-level cost attribution
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a tiled observability pipeline that gives product teams per-route visibility into semantic ranking endpoints (embedding generation, candidate scoring, final re-ranker) including latency percentiles, throughput, batching behavior, KV cache hit rates, and per-request cost breakdown. This ticket scopes the instrumentation design, metric names, sampling strategy for full traces, dashboard wireframes, and alerting thresholds needed for canary rollouts and production SLOs.

Background: Customers and internal teams have asked for concrete cost and quality signals at the route level so they can make trade-offs between higher-quality rerankers and unit economics. Existing platform metrics are high-level (service-level qps/latency) and don't attribute GPU token cost or per-stage latency to routes that share inference pools. We also need better tracing to correlate degraded quality with latency/cold-start/batch-size changes.

Scope & deliverables:
- Metrics design doc with canonical metric names for each stage: embed.gen_latency_ms, embed.kv_cache_hit, candidate.score_ms, reranker.latency_ms, reranker.confidence_histogram, route.request_cost_tokens, route.request_cost_usd.
- Tracing plan: distributed spans for request.receive -> routing -> batching -> model.exec -> postprocess with sampling at 1% for full traces and 50% for high-latency/error paths. Include an example trace template to show per-span attributes (route, model_id, seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit).
- Dashboards: per-route tiles for p50/p90/p99 latency, token-cost per request, cost-per-1000-requests, batch-size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, error rate, and quality regression indicators (synthetic probe pass-rate).
- Alerting: SLO breaches for route p99 > 500ms, cost-per-request increase > 30% vs baseline (7d rolling), synthetic probe failure rate > 5% for 1h.
- Data pipeline changes: tag ingestion to include route_id and model_variant; retention policy for traces and high-cardinality route tags.
- Canary/runbook: checklist for validating tracking during canary rollouts, automated checks before promoting rerank models.

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Cardinality: many customer-defined routes risk exploding metrics. Plan to limit high-cardinality labels (route_id hashed to 8 chars for metrics) and route_name for dashboards only.
- Cost vs fidelity: full-span traces are expensive; we propose sampled full traces and enriched low-overhead metrics.
- Backwards compatibility: keep old service-level metrics intact and add route-scoped variants with opt-in labeling for customers on Dedicated/Private clusters.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: end-to-end billing export changes, console UI polish beyond wireframes, and model-level quality review automation (will be separate initiative).

acceptance_criteria: Stage metrics are emitting with route tags in staging for three representative routes and retained for 30 days.
Dashboards show p50/p90/p99 latency, token-cost, batch-size distribution, and KV cache hit rate per route.
Tracing sampling configured and a sample of full traces is visible in tracing UI with required span attributes.
Alerting rules fire on synthetic probe failures and cost/latency regressions in staging and test alerts are validated.
Runbook for canary promotion includes automated checks for metric drift and synthetic probe pass-rate.
Documentation updated on internal docs and console feature flag documented for Dedicated/Private customers.
